mission_1.flow: When an interaction starts with the display showing that it is listening and we can type our command/request. When no command has been entered it times out and no action is taken. This is good because if no action has been entered it prevents anything from happening. Then when a command was entered like, "bring the blue cup" it lets the user know what it heard and asks it to confirm or correct the command. This lets us see if it is properly hearing our request and allows us to edit if there is any problem. Without confirmation no action is taken, which is the safest decision that could be made. After confirming it lets you know that the action is confirmed and then lets you know when it is complete and then waits for any other commands.  Each distinct cue lets the person know what is going on at all times which is very helpful.
mission_1.predictions: I predict that a point of confusion would be when there is a very vague action given or if the confirmation command is given too late. With a vague command I would expect there to be a state where it asks to clarify or maybe even an error would come up because it needs more information. For a delayed confirmation if it times out then it would support my prediction.
mission_1.safety: The stop completely shuts down and stops what is currently happening, whether there is action being done or not. So, if it is in the middle of completing a task or asking for confirmation it stops motion and task execution. Timeout is there so that the robot will never act on a stale request or one that wasn't confirmed. Without timeout the robot could act on a action that is no longer valid causing even more problems. Cancellation cancels the request and waits for a new one, giving the user control on what the robot should execute. Its ambiguity behavior is good because when given vague tasks it asks for a more specific command and gives information that will help the person give a more guided instruction.
